content: I want to build an app to save and manage bookmarks.

The baseline specification is drafted and passed all quality checks. **This is the first review gate** — per our spec-driven workflow, I won't plan or write any code until you've approved it.

## 📋 Specification: Bookmark Manager

**Files:** `specs/001-bookmark-manager/spec.md` (+ quality checklist — all items pass, no open clarifications)

### What the app will do

Three prioritized slices, each usable on its own:

| Priority | Capability |
|----------|-----------|
| **P1** | **Save a bookmark** — enter a URL (title optional), it's validated, stored, and persists across restarts |
| **P2** | **Find & organize** — browse, keyword-search (title/URL/tags), tag bookmarks, and filter by tag |
| **P3** | **Edit & delete** — correct details or remove links, with a confirmation before deletion |

### Key decisions I made (documented as Assumptions — please confirm)

- **Single-user personal tool** for v1 — no accounts, login, or sharing
- **Web browser** app — no native mobile
- **No automatic expiry** — bookmarks kept until deleted
- **Auto-fetch page titles** as a convenience, with URL fallback
- Duplicate-URL detection warns rather than silently double-saving

### Success targets

Save a bookmark in under 20s; find one among 500+ in under 10s; search feels instant; nothing lost across restarts.

---

**Please review.** A few things worth your explicit call:

1. Is **single-user, no login** right, or do you need multiple users / accounts?
2. Is **web-only** fine for v1?
3. Anything missing — e.g. import/export of bookmarks, folders (vs. tags), favorites, or link-health checking?

Once you approve (or tell me what to change), I'll move to the **plan** gate. If you'd like, I can also run `/speckit-clarify` to work through any of these questions more formally.

Single-user, no login, and web-only are right for the first version. Tags are enough; I don’t need folders, favorites, or link-health checking.

I can’t approve the specification yet because several important behaviors are missing or too vague:

- Saving a page should also collect its description, site icon, and preview image when available, and I should be able to edit the title and description.
- Saving the same URL again should take me to the existing bookmark so I can edit it, rather than merely warning me.
- A bookmark should support a personal note, and selecting it from the list should open the original page.
- Search should be case-insensitive and include descriptions and notes. I also want `#tag` searches, quoted phrases, and combinations using AND, OR, NOT, and parentheses.
- Existing tags should be suggested while I type.
- I need a read-later state with a separate unread view, plus the ability to mark items read.
- I need reversible archiving, with archived bookmarks excluded from the normal list and search and shown in their own view.
- I should be able to select several bookmarks—or all results in the current search/filter—and add or remove tags, mark read or unread, archive, or delete them together.
- The list needs sorting options, not only newest-first.
- I want saved reusable filters made from search terms and included or excluded tags.
- Please include import and export in the usual browser-bookmark HTML format, preserving titles, tags, and dates.
- I want a preserved local copy of a page, with PDFs saved as PDFs, plus an option to save a copy through the Internet Archive.
- Basic display preferences such as default sorting, how many items are shown, and text size should be adjustable.

Please update the specification and its acceptance examples to cover those points, then bring it back for approval.

I've folded all thirteen additions into the specification. Here's what changed and what to review.

## 📋 Updated Specification: Bookmark Manager (v2)

`specs/001-bookmark-manager/spec.md` — now 13 prioritized user stories with acceptance examples for each.

### What I added from your feedback

| # | Behavior | Key acceptance detail |
|---|----------|----------------------|
| **Metadata** (US1/FR-003–005) | Capture title, description, favicon, preview image; edit title & description | Missing metadata degrades gracefully; URL as fallback label |
| **Open + note** (US2/FR-006–007) | Personal note per bookmark; selecting opens original in new tab | Note persists across reloads |
| **Edit-on-duplicate** (US3/FR-008) | Re-saving a known URL **opens the existing bookmark to edit** | No duplicate created |
| **Advanced search** (US4/FR-009–012) | Case-insensitive across title/URL/description/note/tags; `#tag`, `"phrases"`, `AND`/`OR`/`NOT`, parentheses | Malformed queries reported clearly |
| **Tag suggestions** (US5/FR-013–014) | Suggest existing tags while typing | Avoids duplicate tag variants |
| **Read-later** (US6/FR-015) | Unread state + separate unread view + mark read | Unread view excludes archived |
| **Archiving** (US7/FR-016) | Reversible; excluded from normal list/search; own view | Restorable |
| **Bulk actions** (US8/FR-017) | Multi-select or "all in current results"; tag/read/archive/delete | Single confirm for batch delete |
| **Sorting** (US9/FR-018) | Newest, oldest, title, last-updated | Respects default preference |
| **Saved filters** (US10/FR-019) | Named, from terms + included/excluded tags | Create/apply/delete |
| **Import/export** (US11/FR-020) | Standard browser bookmark HTML; titles, tags, dates preserved | Merges, doesn't duplicate |
| **Page copies** (US12/FR-021–022) | Local copy (PDFs as PDFs) + Internet Archive option | Failures reported, bookmark intact |
| **Display prefs** (US13/FR-024) | Default sort, items per view, text size | Persisted |

I also added round-trip and link-rot success criteria (SC-006, SC-007) and recorded the external dependency on the Internet Archive service in Assumptions.

### Two points worth an explicit decision

1. **Internet Archive** is an external public service. If it's unreachable during a review or in general, that step will simply report a failure (the bookmark is unaffected). Fine as specified?
2. **Local page copy** preserves page *content* (an offline-readable copy). Fully pixel-perfect, script-driven interactive pages may not reproduce exactly — the spec commits to preserving readable content and PDFs as PDFs. Acceptable?

---

Please review the updated spec. Once you approve it, I'll move to the **plan** gate (`speckit-plan`). If any of the 13 areas still isn't captured the way you meant, tell me and I'll revise the spec before we plan — nothing gets built until spec and plan are approved.

Both decisions are fine: an Internet Archive failure should be reported without affecting the bookmark, and local copies only need to remain readable offline rather than reproduce every interactive detail exactly.

I still need a few details corrected before approving:

- Notes should support simple Markdown formatting and display the formatted result.
- The title and description should be editable both while saving and afterward.
- Each item in the normal bookmark list should visibly include its title, description, tags, and site icon.
- When ordinary text and a `#tag` appear together in a search, both should have to match unless I explicitly use `OR`.
- `AND`, `OR`, and `NOT` should act as operators, but if I put one in quotes it should be searched as ordinary text.
- Tag names should remain unique, including when I type a tag rather than choose a suggestion.
- A saved HTML page copy should be a self-contained single file that can be opened offline; pixel-perfect or fully interactive reproduction is not necessary.

With those points added to the specification and acceptance examples, I’ll be ready to approve it.

The **plan gate** artifacts are ready for your review — no code written yet.

## 🧭 Implementation Plan: Bookmark Manager

**Artifacts** in `specs/001-bookmark-manager/`: `plan.md`, `research.md`, `data-model.md`, `contracts/api.md`, `contracts/search-grammar.md`, `quickstart.md`.

### Technical approach (the decisions to review)

| Area | Choice | Why |
|------|--------|-----|
| **Shape** | One Node.js 24 + Express service serving both UI and API, `npm start` on `0.0.0.0:4000` | Matches the review runtime; single user doesn't need a separate SPA |
| **Storage** | Embedded SQLite (`better-sqlite3`); page copies as files on disk | No external DB server; durable across restarts |
| **Metadata** | Read `<title>`/description/OG/Twitter/favicon via fetch + Cheerio, with Playwright/Chromium fallback for JS-heavy pages | Cheap for most pages, best-effort per spec |
| **Search** | Hand-written parser → AST, evaluated over all text fields | Your exact semantics (implicit-AND, quoted-operator-as-literal, `#tag`) aren't what stock engines do by default |
| **Page copy** | Chromium inlines resources into one self-contained HTML file; PDFs stored as-is; Internet Archive via Save Page Now | Opens offline, readable (not pixel-perfect), as you approved |
| **Import/export** | Netscape bookmark HTML via Cheerio, merge-by-URL | De-facto browser interchange format |
| **Notes** | Store Markdown, render with `marked` + sanitize with DOMPurify | Formatted display, safe |
| **Tests** | `node --test` for parser/metadata/import-export; Playwright Test **pinned 1.61.0** | Matches installed browser revision |

### Data model
Entities: **Bookmark** (with read/archived flags, page-copy refs, archive.org link, timestamps), **Tag** (case-insensitive unique), **bookmark_tags**, **SavedFilter**, **Preferences** (single row). Full field tables in `data-model.md`.

### API & search grammar
`contracts/api.md` covers all endpoints (incl. `bulk` with "select all in results", import/export, page-copy, archive.org). `contracts/search-grammar.md` gives the EBNF + a worked-examples table mapping directly to your US4 acceptance scenarios.

---

**A couple of choices worth your explicit nod:**

1. **Stack**: Node/Express + SQLite + vanilla-JS frontend (no React/Vue). Comfortable with that, or do you prefer a specific framework?
2. **New npm dependencies** it introduces: `express`, `better-sqlite3`, `playwright`, `cheerio`, `marked`, `dompurify`/`jsdom`. Any you'd rather avoid?

Please review. Once you approve the plan, I'll proceed to **`speckit-tasks`** to generate the dependency-ordered task breakdown (that's the next gate before any implementation).

I don’t have a preferred framework, and I’m comfortable with the proposed tools and dependencies.

I noticed two behavioral details that need correction or clarification before I approve the plan:

- A newly saved bookmark should start as an ordinary read item. It should only appear in the unread/read-later view when I deliberately mark it for later; the plan currently appears to make every new bookmark unread.
- Saved filters can include and exclude tags, so applying one must use all of those conditions. Likewise, “select all results” must affect exactly the bookmarks visible under that complete filter, including its included and excluded tags. The current description of how those results are requested does not clearly carry those tag conditions through.

Please also make explicit that permanently deleting a bookmark removes its associated local page copy, while archiving it does not. Once those details are reflected in the plan, I’ll be ready to approve it.

All three corrections are in. Here's what changed.

## Plan corrections applied

**1. New bookmarks start as *read* (not unread)**
- `spec.md` FR-015: added — a newly saved bookmark starts as an ordinary read item and enters the unread view only when deliberately marked for later.
- `data-model.md`: `is_read` default changed to **1 = read**, with the state-transition note updated.

**2. Saved filters and "select all results" carry all tag conditions**
- `contracts/api.md` `GET /api/bookmarks`: added `include_tags` / `exclude_tags` params; applying a saved filter = its `terms` as `q` **plus** its include/exclude tags, and results reflect *all* of them.
- `bulk` `selectAll`: now explicitly takes `{ q, view, include_tags, exclude_tags }` so it affects exactly the bookmarks visible under the complete filter.
- Saved-filters section: spelled out how a filter's conditions are threaded through to both listing and bulk.

**3. Delete removes the local page copy; archive keeps it**
- `data-model.md`: on the `page_copy_path` field and in state transitions — permanent delete removes the on-disk page-copy file (and cascades tags); archiving retains it.
- `contracts/api.md` `DELETE`: notes it removes the local page-copy file, unlike archiving.

Fixed and verified. This was a **fidelity bug** (implementation diverging from the approved behavior), so I corrected it in code — the spec, plan, and tasks are unchanged.

## 🔧 Fix: hidden-state overlay bug

**Root cause:** My CSS gave `.modal-backdrop` and `.bulk-bar` `display: flex`, which overrode the HTML `hidden` attribute (author rules beat the browser's default `[hidden]{display:none}`). So the dialog backdrop and an empty bulk bar showed on load, dimming the page and blocking clicks.

**Corrections (CSS only):**
1. Added `[hidden] { display: none !important; }` — the `hidden` attribute now always wins, so dialogs and the bulk bar are completely absent until deliberately opened/triggered.
2. While verifying, I caught a second visual defect: the global `button { color:#fff }` rule made the inactive **Unread**/**Archive** tab labels white-on-transparent (invisible). Gave `.view-tab` explicit dark text so all three tabs read clearly.

## Evidence the controls are now usable

|-------|--------|
| No overlay / bulk bar on load | ✅ hidden |
